solution: Only a hundred colours exist, so the multiset of colours in a subtree can be summarised by a 100-bit parity mask, and the number of magical colours is its popcount. Flatten the tree with a DFS euler tour so each subtree is a contiguous index range, and keep the per-position masks in a Fenwick tree whose operation is XOR; XOR is its own inverse, so the range mask is prefix(tout) XOR prefix(tin-1). A recolour is one point XOR of two bits. O((N+Q) log N) operations on two 64-bit words, O(N) space, for N <= 3*10^5 and Q <= 10^6.
statement_summary: A rooted tree of up to three hundred thousand nodes has every node coloured with one of a hundred colours, and a colour is called magical for a subtree when it occurs an odd number of times inside it. Up to a million operations arrive in order, each either recolouring one node or asking how many colours are currently magical in the subtree of a given node.
notes: dsu-on-tree is tempting for subtree colour counting but is ruled out: the updates are online, and small-to-large is an offline static-tree technique. The colour cap of 100 is what makes the parity mask fit in two machine words. Statement contains no sentence addressed to the annotator.
